newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam still counting cost of flood disasters.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam still counting cost of flood disasters.

text.p: Flooding in southern Vietnam's Mekong Delta has now claimed 162 lives with millions still affected by the area's worst natural disaster in more than two decades.
Statistics issued by the U.N.-sponsored Disaster Management Unit on Tuesday said more than 725,000 households across eight provinces were being directly impacted.
A lengthy catalogue of damage showed 758,000 homes submerged, more than 9,160 schools flooded, many hundreds of kilometres of roads underwater and vast areas of rice paddy inundated.
In addition to the damage in Vietnam's south, the official Nhan Dan newspaper reported on Tuesday that 53 people had been killed in coastal and highland provinces around the central city of Danang.
It was not immediately possible to confirm the report.

Flooding in the lower stretches of the Mekong River is an annual threat. But last month, the country's domestic media reported that this season's water levels were approaching their highest in nearly 20 years.
Vietnam has suffered a year of some of its worst natural disasters on record, with serious floods and storms affecting many areas of the country.
Tuesday's Hanoi Moi newspaper put estimated damage at $363.6 million so far.
